controls: Round1 high-value 37/37 normalization complete does not imply breadth closure.
CANONICAL_MAJOR_REGION is a navigation-anchor concept, not semantic authority or metaphysical root.
No canonical major region has been admitted.
Coverage crosswalk remains NOT_READY while breadth residuals and admission criteria are pending.

findings.claim: Round 1 high-value candidate normalization is complete: every one of the 37 candidates maps to one or more explicit Round2 identities; four former combined candidates required split repair.
The current normalized graph has no identity-label collisions, no broken topology relations, and no canonical-root self-admissions.
The seven-archetype topology grammar is total over all current normalized role classes and better explains the observed graph than a uniform discipline-tree model.

`Canonical root` is the wrong default navigation concept. `Canonical major region` is preferable because stable Atlas anchors need not be primitive ontological roots and may coexist with cross-cutting axes and bridges.
Foundational breadth is still open: the original broad census contains residual candidates not yet normalized even though the Round1 high-value subset is complete.
The next work should target breadth residuals and draft explicit canonical-major-region admission criteria; Ordivon coverage scoring remains premature until that audit passes.

navigationModel.reason: The graph contains domains, bridges, axes, infrastructure, applied/translational areas and composites. Calling every navigation anchor a root incorrectly implies one ontological tree and one semantic node type.

negativeConclusions: Do not restore a fixed root count.
Do not reinterpret CANONICAL_MAJOR_REGION as semantic authority or metaphysical fundamentality.
Do not admit a major region from institutional independence alone.
Do not force BRIDGE/AXIS/INFRASTRUCTURE identities beneath one parent region.
Do not treat high-value-subset completion as whole foundational-space closure.

archetypes.APPLIED_TRANSLATIONAL: Intervention, realization, professional or translational area that consumes foundations and may contain foundational cores.
archetypes.AXIS: Cross-cutting organizing dimension such as inference, process, dynamics, measurement, design or integration.
archetypes.BRIDGE: Stable identity whose meaning intrinsically connects multiple domains.
archetypes.COMPOSITE: Stable field assembled from several distinct domains/methods, often historically or institutionally coherent.
archetypes.DOMAIN: Stable major area of inquiry organized around objects, regimes, concepts, systems, temporal evidence, or other coherent subject matter.
archetypes.INFRASTRUCTURE: Research/epistemic capability that enables inquiry without being an object-domain.
archetypes.MAJOR_SUBSPACE: Large coherent region within or across domains; not presumed a canonical navigation anchor.

topologyGrammar.rule: Archetype is orthogonal to navigation-anchor admission; one identity may carry multiple archetypes.
